# ADR-1108: Dependencies install at Setup and live in per-lock sets

## Status

accepted

## Context

Every Cortex hook runs scripts/launcher.py and, until this decision, every one called ensure_deps: an install whenever the stamp (digest of uv.lock, Python minor) did not match. Hook budgets are 5 to 30 s; measured 2026-10-14 the uv bootstrap takes 29.3 s, the base set 28.5 s (ADR-1104), a cold SessionStart 109 s. A hook the host cancels mid-install leaves a scratch directory: the owner's plugin data held 64 deps.tmp-<pid> directories (3 on 10-10, 8 on 12th, 19 on 13th, 34 on 14th), each holding only uv's .lock. ADR-1104 raised the SessionStart timeout to 300 s so the hook could install; an earlier draft of this decision (numbered 1106, never merged; that number belongs to another change) removed the install from every hook and let the first session after an install or a lock change start with 'Cortex not ready'. The owner rejected both (2026-10-15): 'it must start with everything ready, not delete or wait for an eternity': no session may start with Cortex not ready, and none may wait on an install.

Host facts, measured on Claude Code 2.1.300 (raw: ~/.claude/fleet/deps-out-of-hook/lab, real): (1) a plugin 'Setup' hook runs only for 'claude --init-only' (or --init/--maintenance), synchronously, before the SessionStart:startup hook that --init-only also runs; it needs no login; CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA are set. (2) The host shows none of its output, in a pipe or a pty, and 'claude --init-only' exits 0 whatever the hook did (exit 1 and 2 tried); a failure is visible only with --debug-file. (3) With no timeout field the host killed a Setup hook 599 s after it started; an explicit timeout field is honoured. (4) 'claude plugin update' refreshes the marketplace clone and applies the update in one command (the clone's uv.lock and cache/<version> change together). (5) A third-party marketplace's autoUpdate defaults to false (only the official set defaults on), so the common update is that command, run by the user. (6) Plugin data (<config>/plugins/data/<id>) is outside the versioned plugin root and survives updates; installed_plugins.json lists every installed copy; known_marketplaces.json gives the clone, which for this plugin (source './') is the plugin tree itself. (7) PreToolUse: exit 2 blocks the tool call, any other non-zero code continues it (the host's own hook help text). Not observed: the order of the interactive startup autoupdate pass (marketplace refresh, plugin update, in-session reload) relative to SessionStart; a throwaway config has no login and the pass did not run under --init-only. The binary names the steps (marketplaces_refreshed, then plugins_updated, 'reloaded for this session').

uv.lock records the plugin's own version, so its digest changed at 28 of 37 release transitions (v4.0.0 to v4.23.5) although the dependency set changed at 8 of 29 (v4.9.0 to v4.23.5; none from v4.22.0 to v4.23.5), measured with git show <tag>:uv.lock.

## Decision

1. Sets are keyed. Installed dependencies live in <data>/sets/<key>/ (and the <key>.* sidecars: locks, stamps, setup outcome, users), key = first 16 hex of sha256(uv.lock with the project's own 'version' line removed) (scripts/launcher_layout.py). Two plugin versions locking one dependency set share one directory; a different set is a different directory, so installing the next version's set never touches the set a running session imports from. The managed CPython, the bootstrapped uv and the logs are shared in <data>.

2. Setup installs everything, in the foreground. The plugin registers a Setup hook (scripts/launcher.py --setup) with an explicit timeout of 1800 s (the launcher's own lock bound; the host default of 600 s is shorter than a slow network's install). It installs the base set and the semantic-search set from uv.lock and downloads the pinned embedding model (the operator's CORTEX_EMBEDDING_ZERO_DOWNLOAD opt-out still skips the last two), stamps the sets, records {status, error} in <key>.setup.json and appends everything it prints to <data>/setup.log. Because the host discards that output and its exit code, the documented install runs scripts/init_plugin.py (README, install_e2e): it runs 'claude --init-only', shows the log as it grows, then reads the recorded outcome and exits 1 with the cause unless it says ready. It finds the plugin through 'claude plugin list --json' (installPath) and the data directory by the host's naming, <config>/plugins/data/<id with characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] replaced by '-'>; plain 'claude --init-only' also installs, silently.

3. No other hook installs (kept from the earlier draft; supersedes ADR-1104 decision 4, the 300 s SessionStart install). A hook returns from the launcher only when the base set of its key is stamped (launcher_deps.set_ready, no subprocess). Otherwise it exits non-zero within about 0.1 s (measured) with 'Cortex not ready: <cause>', the log and the command that installs now, and starts at most one detached --install-base-job (job lock). The PreToolUse gates (decision_gate, no_deps_gate) exit 2 in that case: they fail closed, the message says how to leave (run 'claude --init-only', or wait for the job), and the edit that was refused can be retried. A failed job leaves a failure stamp for its key; a hook then reports the failure and starts no job (no retry per hook call; the stamp clears when an install of that set succeeds). The detached logs rotate past 1 MiB. SessionStart is back to 30 s in the Claude and Codex manifests. The Codex plugin runs hooks through plugins/hypermnesia-mcp-codex/scripts/runtime.py, which only execs an already installed wheel and raises 'run runtime.py setup first' otherwise: it cannot install, and its 30 s timeout bounds nothing it does.

4. The next version's set is installed ahead of its update, and old sets are removed, by one detached job. SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit call launcher_maintain.start_if_needed: three small JSON files and at most three uv.lock hashes, no install. When the marketplace clone (the single seam launcher_installed.next_tree) holds a different plugin version whose key has no stamped set, or an installed set is unreferenced, it starts --maintain-job, which runs the CLONE's own launcher with --setup (so the clone's uv.lock and project define the set) and then collects. A set is kept while its key is the running version's, an installed copy's or the clone's, or while a live MCP server registered itself as its user (<key>.users/<pid>); with any unreadable record nothing is removed. The flat deps/ directory of the earlier layout is removed once the running version's own set is installed.

5. The cleanup tool (launcher.py --cleanup-deps) audits and removes the sets/ directory and the legacy deps/ of other plugin identities.

## Consequences

Positive: after 'claude plugin install' + 'claude --init-only' the first session starts ready (measured, throwaway config: Setup 307 s cold including 865 MB of sets and the model, progress visible through init_plugin.py; the next --init-only: Setup 9.6 s, SessionStart status 0 in 606 ms, 'Cortex ready: ... semantic search on'). No hook is cancelled mid-install, so no scratch is orphaned. A release that leaves the dependency set alone (21 of 29) finds its set installed with no step at all. Failure of the install is no longer silent for the documented path (init_plugin.py exits 1 with the cause) and not repeated per hook.

RESIDUAL, measured and not solved here: the first session after an update that changes the dependency set (8 of 29 releases) still finds its set missing, because 'claude plugin update' refreshes the clone and applies the update in one command, so the pre-install of point 4 has no moment before the update unless a session of the current version is running when the clone is refreshed (a second terminal, or the interactive autoupdate pass if the marketplace enabled it and it refreshes while a session lives). The sequence: claude plugin update (no session running) -> next session: SessionStart exits 1 'Cortex not ready' in 0.09 s, the PreToolUse gates exit 2, one background install starts; the MCP server's own stand-in serves tools while it installs (ADR-1104); the next session after the job finishes is ready. 'claude --init-only' after the update makes it ready first. Whether to accept this, to refresh and pre-install from the git remote independently of the host, or to ask the host for an update event is a product decision left to the owner.

Negative, known: Setup output and exit code are invisible to the host's own users (the wrapper is the visible path); the first install is a foreground wait by design, in the one command meant for it; a session idle for a long time on a superseded set keeps it (the registry only sees live processes); a pre-PR plugin version still running keeps using deps/, which the first collection removes. A hook on Python below 3.10 with no managed CPython exits non-zero the same way until Setup or the job has installed it.
